per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window at the tails and the end of helix III. RelaxDB source paper now read in full (286 K, pH 4.3, 0.8 mM, 11.7 T, DNA-free): overall tau_m 10.51 ns (MF) or about 9.85 ns (RSDM); Arg1-Leu7, Arg58, Gln59 and Ala60-Gln67 move much faster than the core, Arg53 is intermediate and looks like a hinge, and the three helices Gln10-Gln22, Ala28-Ile38 and Thr43-Gln50 stay ordered (R15521-J3). The paper's own 10 ns MD reproduces this picture (J9, md_only).
per_window.us-ms: unresolved by the single-field Rex rule: exchange is detected in the reference state but carries no population. Tyr25 (entry 26) has R2 26.39 s-1 against 8.41-16.53 s-1 elsewhere and is the only fitted model-free Rex, with J(0) far above every other residue (J1); RSDM alone adds Lys21, Gln22, Ile38 and His52 (entry 22, 23, 39, 53) from the J(omega_N)-J(0) correlation (J2). One field, no dispersion, no rate, population or Delta-omega.
per_window.slower_than_ms: unresolved, abstract only. Amide H/D exchange rates point to a local fluctuation at N51-R53 (J5, r3).
per_window.undetermined: Helix III extension 51-59 less rigid with a kink at 51-53 (J4, r2); protease resistance of the C terminus at neutral pH (J6) and its increased accessibility after DNA binding (J7); DNA-bound human NKX2-1 crystal (J8); the paper's own 10 ns MD (J9). Not judged: r4 (database survey of other proteins), r5 (equilibrium thermal unfolding by CD/DSC at pH 5.0), r6 and r7 (3.5 ns MD of modelled DNA complexes, abstract only, no dynamics result).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Probably yes at one site, without a rate: in the free rat TTF-1 homeodomain at 286 K, pH 4.3, 0.8 mM, 11.7 T, Tyr25 (entry Y26) carries a slow-exchange contribution in both the model-free and the spectral-density analysis, with R2 26.39 s-1 against 8.41-16.53 s-1 for every other residue, and the spectral-density analysis alone adds Lys21, Gln22, Ile38 and His52 at the helix ends; the measurement is single-field with no dispersion, so no rate, population or chemical-shift difference exists, and the authors offer aromatic side-chain motion and helix-end fraying as interpretations.
protein_summary.deposition_readback: Deposition-derived; same numbers RelaxDB labels were computed from; not literature confirmation. BMRB 15521 holds 500 MHz T1, T2 and NOE for 65 residues with metadata pH 4.3 and 286 K, and the paper itself names BMRB 15521 as the deposition of its chemical shift and relaxation data (p. 445). R2/R1 above 8.08 flags K22, Q23 and I39 (author K21, Q22, I38), three of the four RSDM-only exchange residues. Y26 (author Y25) has the largest R2, 26.3 s-1 against about 12-14 s-1 in the helices, but NOE 0.53, so the screen calls it fast; H53 (author H52) has NOE 0.63. NOE below 0.65 marks R2-L8, H53, R54 and M57-Q68 plus L17, K25-L27, E31, M38 and Q45. Median R2/R1 over NOE >= 0.65 residues (7.2) gives about 9.5 ns by the rigid-rotor formula, near the abstract's 9.85-10.51 ns.
open_conflicts: C-terminal region: mobile by NMR at pH 4.3 and 286 K (R15521-J3) versus protease-inaccessible at neutral pH (J6, r9); the proteolysis abstract names the pH difference and the methods measure different things, so this is kept as a condition difference.
questions_for_gina: The deposited R2 of Y26 (26.3 s-1) comes with NOE 0.53, and the paper's p. 438 prints the Tyr25 exchange-related quantity as '14.67 +/- 2.35 ns', a unit that cannot be an exchange rate: should the atlas treat Y25 as exchange, as the authors do, or as a mixed fast-motion and exchange site?
protein_summary.buffer_note: The RelaxDB source paper (doi:10.1111/j.1742-4658.2007.06208.x) was read in full on 2026-10-20 (case S6_r6_15521_20261020220843), superseding the abstract-only row R15521-r1, which is no longer cited; the other rat-domain rows (r2, r3, r5-r7, r9, r10) remain abstracts. The sample has no buffer salt: pH 4.3 was set with HCl and is an uncorrected meter reading, at 286 K, where the domain is stable; proteolysis was done at neutral pH and calorimetry at pH 5.0, and the domain unfolds at 32 °C without salt (r5), so temperature, salt and pH all matter. Glu17, Leu34 and Lys46 were excluded for NOE overlap and Pro29 and Pro42 have no amide. The authors question their own per-residue local correlation times and name Tyr54 as a possible numerical artefact; supplementary Tables S1-S4 were unavailable, so per-residue relaxation values were not reconstructed. The second read left r2 unverified only for the claim of exact sequence identity to 1FTT:A; the PDF adjudication (ledger/adjudication_pdf_batch2.json) confirmed the five exchange residues, the R2 values and the conditions from the rendered pages.

judgments.reason: Full text of the RelaxDB source paper: Tyr25 is the one residue to which both analyses assign a slow-exchange contribution, with R2 26.39 s-1 where the rest of the domain lies between 8.41 and 16.53 s-1; exchange is detected in the reference state, but the measurement is at a single field with no rate, population or chemical-shift difference, and single-field Rex can also come from anisotropic tumbling; a dispersion experiment would confirm (sources_cache/10.1111_j.1742-4658.2007.06208.x.pdf, pp. 435, 437-438, 440-443).

detection.observable: S2 and spectral densities; overall tau_m 10.51 +/- 0.05 ns by model-free and 9.85 +/- 1.79 ns (J(omega_N)-J(0)) or 9.84 +/- 0.20 ns (J(0.87omega_H)-J(0)) by RSDM, with a generalised internal correlation time of 0.28 +/- 0.11 ns

judgments.reason: Full text: both analyses place the terminal segments Arg1-Leu7 and Ala60-Gln67, plus Arg58 and Gln59 at the end of helix III, towards much shorter effective correlation times than the structured core, with Arg53 intermediate, so the C-terminal part of the recognition helix and the tails move on the sub-nanosecond scale while the three helices stay ordered; the authors warn that their per-residue local correlation times are unreliable because internal and overall motion may not separate (sources_cache/10.1111_j.1742-4658.2007.06208.x.pdf, pp. 436-443, Tables 1-2, Figs. 3-4).
